Factspilot.com – European Media Network

MinBy™ | Denmark

Journalism · Fact-checking · Artificial Intelligence · European Cooperation

WORK WITH US FROM YOUR OWN EU COUNTRY

Are you an experienced journalist, freelance journalist or media project manager living in an EU country outside Denmark?
Do you have professional knowledge of your national media industry, established contacts and an interest in international journalism?

We would like to hear from you.
MinBy™ is seeking experienced and independent media professionals to help establish and develop Factspilot.com, an international media and technology initiative.
Our ambition is to build a European network of locally based journalists, media professionals and project coordinators working together across national borders.
We are particularly interested in candidates who already understand their own country's media landscape and can contribute from the beginning.
You will work from your own country. Relocation to Denmark is not required.

ABOUT FACTSPILOT.COM
Factspilot.com is an international initiative developed by MinBy™, a Danish digital media network comprising 1,522 ultra-local media outlets across Denmark's 98 municipalities, alongside a portfolio of specialised digital magazine concepts.

Factspilot aims to develop a scalable European media infrastructure combining:

• 
Independent journalism and news production.

• 
Fact-checking, source verification and documentation.

• 
Artificial intelligence and editorial technology.

• 
Automated translation and multilingual publishing.

• 
International news collection and distribution.

• 
Cooperation between journalists and media organisations across Europe.

Our ambition is to connect national and local journalistic expertise with a shared international platform.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

We are recruiting candidates with experience in one or more of the following areas.

1. FREELANCE JOURNALISTS / MEDIA PARTNERS

We are looking for experienced freelance journalists interested in contributing to Factspilot's development in their own countries.

Your potential responsibilities include:

• 
Researching and producing journalistic content.

• 
Identifying reliable national and regional news sources.

• 
Conducting fact-checking and source verification.

• 
Establishing relationships with local journalists, editors and newsrooms.

• 
Contributing to cross-border journalism and multilingual publishing.

• 
Helping develop Factspilot's national media network.

You may already be working independently, seeking new assignments or interested in becoming part of a larger international media initiative.

You do not need to own a company to apply.

2. JOURNALISTS / EDITORS / MEDIA PROFESSIONALS

We are seeking journalists and media professionals with practical experience and strong knowledge of their national media environment.

Relevant backgrounds include:

• 
Journalism and editorial production.

• 
Investigative journalism and research.

• 
Fact-checking and verification.

• 
Digital publishing and news distribution.

• 
Editorial coordination and media development.

We particularly value candidates who understand their country's media structures, professional standards and relevant sources.

3. MEDIA PROJECT MANAGERS / NATIONAL COORDINATORS

We are also seeking experienced project managers who can contribute to establishing and coordinating Factspilot's activities in their own countries.

Your potential responsibilities include:

• 
Identifying relevant journalists and media contacts.

• 
Building national professional networks.

• 
Developing international cooperation opportunities.

• 
Coordinating local project activities.

• 
Contributing to project planning, budgets and implementation.

• 
Supporting European partnerships and potential funding applications.

Experience with international media projects, European cooperation or EU funding programmes is an advantage.

YOUR LOCAL EXPERIENCE IS OUR PRIORITY

We are particularly interested in applicants who:

• 
Live in an EU Member State outside Denmark.

• 
Have professional experience in journalism, media or project management.

• 
Understand their national media industry.

• 
Have relevant professional contacts and relationships.

• 
Speak and write the language of their country fluently.

• 
Can communicate professionally in English.

• 
Work independently and take responsibility for results.

• 
Are comfortable using modern digital tools and AI-supported workflows.

• 
Are interested in international cooperation and long-term project development.

An established professional network and practical experience may be more important than formal qualifications.

EUROPEAN PROJECT DEVELOPMENT

Factspilot is exploring opportunities for international project financing, including the European Union's Creative Europe – Journalism Partnerships programme.

Selected candidates may contribute to the development of European cooperation projects, including the identification of national partners, editorial activities and project coordination.

Experience with EU programmes or international project funding is particularly relevant for project management candidates, but is not required for journalists.

WHAT WE OFFER

We offer the opportunity to participate in the development of an ambitious international media initiative from an early stage.

Depending on your professional background and the project's development, opportunities may include:

• 
Journalism and editorial assignments.

• 
Fact-checking and research activities.

• 
National media coordination.

• 
International project development.

• 
Participation in European media cooperation.

• 
Longer-term professional collaboration.

You will have the opportunity to contribute your existing expertise while working from your own country.

WORK LOCATION AND EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS

Location: Your country of residence within the European Union, excluding Denmark.
Work arrangement: Remote, with activities carried out locally in your own country.
Professional profiles: Journalists, freelance journalists, editors, media professionals and project managers.
Employment and cooperation: Depending on the role, opportunities may include employment or paid freelance and project-based assignments.

Working hours, responsibilities, remuneration and contractual terms will be agreed individually before any engagement begins.

Factspilot is currently in a development phase. The availability and commencement of specific assignments depend on project progress and financing.

Applicants may be unemployed, employed or self-employed. A registered company is not required.

APPLICATION AND SELECTION

We are interested in your professional experience, local knowledge, independence and ability to contribute to Factspilot's development.

Please include the following information in your application:

• 
Country of residence – Where do you currently live and work?

• 
Professional profile – Journalist, freelance journalist, media professional or project manager?

• 
Experience – What is your relevant professional background?

• 
Local knowledge – What experience and contacts do you have within your country's media industry?

• 
Contribution – How could you help develop Factspilot in your country?

• 
International experience – Have you previously worked on international or EU-funded projects?

Please include your CV and, where relevant, links to published work, previous projects or professional references.

Selected applicants may be invited to complete a voluntary practical assignment designed to demonstrate relevant skills, independent thinking and professional initiative.

HOW TO APPLY

Applications must be submitted through MinBy™'s digital recruitment system.

Apply here:

https://minbymedie.dk/ansogning-formular/

We welcome applications from qualified candidates throughout the 26 EU Member States outside Denmark.

Role Overview

The High School Psychologist / Social-Emotional Counsellor is a member of the Student Support Team and shares responsibility for student wellbeing, inclusion and mental health across the High School. The role provides direct counselling, psychological support, consultation, and system-level guidance to students, families and staff, with particular attention to students who are socially, emotionally or psychologically vulnerable. Working hours and days are flexible and can be arranged to fit your existing schedule. You have the freedom to allocate your working hours across the week in a way that suits your availability while meeting the needs of students and the school.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Provide individual social-emotional counselling to students aged 15–19, supporting their mental health, resilience, relationships and academic wellbeing.

• 
Design and implement preventive and systemic interventions at class and year-group levels to promote student wellbeing and positive group dynamics.

• 
Develop, implement and review individual student support plans in alignment with the IB Access and Inclusion Policy.

• 
Collaborate with the student wellbeing team, student support staff, teachers and parents to coordinate appropriate support.

• 
Guide students and families through the Danish public and private healthcare and youth support systems, including PPR, specialist clinics and pathways to diagnostic assessment.

• 
Prepare professional referrals and supporting documentation for external assessments, including neuropsychological or psychiatric evaluations, within the scope of professional competence.

• 
Follow safeguarding, confidentiality and data protection requirements; identify students requiring specialist intervention and coordinate appropriate follow-up and support.

Qualifications and Experience

• 
Relevant qualifications and training in psychology, counselling or social-emotional support. A qualification as a psychologist, including assessment and diagnosis, is preferred; demonstrated expertise in social-emotional counselling will also be considered.

• 
Knowledge of the Danish healthcare and youth support systems, including PPR.

• 
Experience with psychological screening and assessment tools such as WISC, WAIS, BASC, and BRIEF is an advantage.

• 
Experience working within the International Baccalaureate (IB) system is desirable but not required.

Position Details

• 
Reports to: High School Principal / Programme Principal

• 
Works closely with: the Learning Support Team, Student Wellbeing Team, teaching staff, parents and external specialists

• 
Position: Part-time (50%)

• 
Start date: January 2027, or by agreement

• 
Closing date for applications: 20 November 2026

About Driversnote

Driversnote is a profitable, product-led SaaS company based in Copenhagen that helps over 4.5 million users simplify mileage tracking, with paying customers in 100+ countries. Our core product is a freemium mobile app, often paired with our iBeacon hardware for precise, automated mileage logging, and backed by a powerful web platform.

We’re a close-knit team of 50 working together across design, mobile and web development, marketing, support, sales and customer success. We’ve quadrupled our ARR in the last three years by staying focused on delivering real value to our users, and we’re now expanding from B2C into B2B, building advanced features for teams.

Our Customer Success and Support team is locally anchored in Denmark, Canada and Australia. Customers get help in their own time zone from people who know their market, its rules and how its businesses work.

The role

As Customer Success Manager for EMEA, you own a portfolio of our larger business customers and make sure they get real value from Driversnote, renew, and grow.

This is an outcome-led role, not a usage-monitoring one. Teams today can build their own tracking or buy a system that includes it, so we win by helping customers save money, stay compliant and run their mileage process with less effort. You’ll be the person who makes that happen for your accounts.

Success looks like this after your first year:

• 
Your accounts renew, and you know why the few that leave did

• 
New accounts are live and in use within weeks, not months

• 
Your accounts grow in licences and use more of what we offer

• 
Customers see you as a trusted adviser on mileage, reimbursement and compliance, and Driversnote is built into how they work, from their mileage policy to their payroll and AI tools

What you’ll do

• 
Own retention and renewals. Manage renewals for your accounts from start to finish, spot risk early and act on it.

• 
Get new accounts live. Run onboarding for new teams, with kickoffs for admins, managers and drivers, so the first year sets them up for success.

• 
Grow your accounts. Find expansion opportunities where it makes sense, help teams roll out to more drivers and pass qualified leads to Sales.

• 
Lead outcome-focused reviews. Run annual and quarterly business reviews built around what customers achieve, not just how much they use the app.

• 
Be the expert. Advise customers on mileage reimbursement policy, tax compliance and audit-readiness in your markets.

• 
Get Driversnote deeper into their processes. Help customers improve how they handle mileage end to end: shaping their mileage policy, connecting Driversnote to payroll, finance and AI tools, and removing manual steps, so we become part of how they work, not just an app they use.

• 
Help shape new services. Work with us as we build new offers, such as fleet mileage reports, CO2 reporting and compliance checks.

• 
Keep the data clean. Use HubSpot, health scores and AI tools to manage your portfolio, and log why customers leave so we can learn from it.

• 
Be the customer’s voice. Share what you hear with Product, Sales and Support to improve the product.

What we’re looking for

• 
A few years’ experience in customer success, account management or implementation, ideally in B2B SaaS

• 
Experience owning renewals or a revenue target, or helping customers get live with a new system

• 
Native or near-native English, written and spoken, since many of our customers are in the UK

• 
A commercial mindset: you can turn a customer’s goals into a reason to renew and grow

• 
Comfortable with data, CRM tools and AI; you use numbers to spot risk and show value

• 
A real interest in using AI to create more value, not just to work faster. We take AI seriously here, not as a buzzword: you’ll use and help shape the AI agents and workflows our team relies on every day

• 
Clear, warm communication with everyone from drivers to finance directors

• 
The role is based in our Copenhagen office, and you need a valid permit to work in Denmark

Nice to have

• 
Experience with expansion and upsell in existing accounts

• 
Additional languages are a plus

• 
Knowledge of mileage reimbursement, fleet management, payroll or tax compliance

• 
Experience with HubSpot

This role is probably not for you if…

• 
You want to stay at a strategic distance. This is a hands-on role: you’ll run onboardings, dig into data, fix problems and talk to drivers as well as finance directors.

• 
You only want large accounts. Your portfolio will be a mix of smaller teams and large accounts, and you need to enjoy both.

• 
You’re looking for enterprise sales. We don’t do long, complex corporate sales cycles. If large enterprise selling is what drives you, this isn’t the right fit.

What we offer

• 
Ownership from day one: a high-impact role where you own our B2B customers in the EMEA region.

• 
Shape how we do it: help build the B2B success motion for an established, profitable company.

• 
People to learn from: work with a team of highly experienced entrepreneurs and tech people, across Denmark, Canada and Australia.

• 
Growth: a clear career path in Customer Success, with specialisations as our services grow.

• 
Balance: a healthy work-life balance.

• 
Location and benefits: our Copenhagen office, pension and a learning budget.

We work in a relaxed environment in new offices near the Meatpacking District. Every day there’s a tasty, freshly cooked lunch (with a vegetarian option) and great coffee. We also have cosy Friday drinks and great events, from our running club and gaming nights to our epic Christmas and summer parties.

How to apply

Fill out an application here

We review applications and respond to candidates on an ongoing basis, so apply soon. We aim for a start date of 1 December or 1 January, depending on your availability, but finding the right fit matters more to us than a deadline. Expect a case during the interview process: it represents the kind of work you’ll do with us.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Applicants are invited for a double degree PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Biological and Chemical Engineering programme. The position is part of the MSCA project TagTIC - Target mining for the development of therapeutics against pathogen-induced cancers, ID: 101311627, Call: HORIZON-MSCA-2025-DN-01-01. Project website: tagtic.eu

Note that this is a double degree PhD project within an MSCA Joint Doctorate. Under the currently planned arrangement, the candidate will work for approximately three years at TissueGnostics GmbH in Vienna, Austria, and one year at Aarhus University, Denmark.

Research area and project description:

Microbial infections are increasingly recognized as important contributors to cancer, but identifying the spatial tissue features and molecular signatures associated with infection-driven disease remains challenging. Integrating tissue imaging with spatial transcriptomics and microbiome information offers opportunities to characterize disease-associated patterns and improve biomarker discovery.

Consortium: This PhD postion is part of the interdisciplinary TagTIC consortium, which brings together expertise in microbiology, virology, oncology, immunology, medicinal chemistry, imaging, AI, and bioinformatics, with support from associated partners in biotech, diagnostics, and science communication. Its collaborative structure allows doctoral candidates to work within a network where discovery science, technology development, training, and societal impact are closely connected.

Project DC11: This PhD is part of the TagTIC consortium. It combines machine learning with image analysis to support precision oncology. The aim is to develop AI algorithms that integrate tissue imaging, spatial transcriptomics and microbiome data (multiomics) to identify biomarkers and predict disease progression.

jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science invites applications for one-year research assistant positions focused on developing innovative robot control and navigation techniques using simulation-based learning for medical robotic endoscope devices.

  Project Background
 This project addresses two critical challenges in the field of medical robotics to improve patient care through advanced simulation and control:

   	
• Image-Based Navigation: Creating reward functions for scoring navigation policies for medical robotic devices moving inside the human body, relying solely on image information and accounting for environment changes through interaction models. 	
• Soft Robot Control: Developing learning-based methods to control a soft robot endoscope via high-level navigation policies to perform clinical procedures inside the human body, including quality assessment of these methods during in-vivo interventions.   The successful candidates will join a multidisciplinary and collaborative team renowned for cutting-edge research in medical imaging and simulation technologies, operating within a global network across France, Germany, and Spain.

  Roles and Responsibilities
 The successful candidates will play a central role in the project’s technical and scientific success. While the level of autonomy will vary by position, both roles will share the following core responsibilities:

   	
• Technical Development & Implementation: Designing and implementing machine learning methods for motion planning and control. This includes integrating simulation-based learning frameworks and demonstrating the resulting systems on real robotic hardware and soft robot endoscopes. 	
• Research & Scientific Contribution: Contributing to the project’s core objectives by producing impactful research outputs. This includes writing high-quality papers for peer-reviewed journals and presenting findings at international conferences. 	
• Collaboration & Knowledge Exchange: Facilitating collaborations with industrial partners and academic collaborators to ensure that the developed methodologies are meaningful and translatable to real-world clinical practice. 	
• Professional Growth & Mentorship: Engaging in a high-growth research environment. The positions can be extendable and towards a PhD depending on the future funding status. The project has a trackrecord of landing members in top PhD program and faculty positions. 	
• Interdisciplinary Integration: Actively participating in team discussions and workshops to integrate expertise across medical imaging, physics simulation, and robotics control.   Profile
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills

   	
• MSc in the fields mentioned above. 	
• You have a strong foundation and track record in robotics simulation, robot control, computer vision and/or machine learning for physical systems. 	
• You are highgly experienced in numerical optimization algorithms, preferably applied to motion planning or reinforcement learning. Hands-on experience on real robots especially soft robot systems is a plus. 	
• Proficient scientific computing and programming (C++/Python) and experience with libraries such as PyTorch, JAX, Warp, Taichi, or ROS. 	
• Excellent communication skills and a high level of motivation to work in a multidisciplinary, international research environment.   Desireable experience and skills

   	
• Experience in publishing peer-reviewed research in top-tier robotics or AI venues. 	
• Familiarity with physics simulation such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, Newton Physics, SOFA etc.   Terms of employment
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 1 year. The starting date is 15 February or after agreement

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. 

  Questions
 Further information on the Department is linked at http://www.science.ku.dk/english/about-the-faculty/organisation/. Inquiries about the positions can be made to kenny@di.ku.dk and hayi@di.ku.dk.

  Application procedure

   	
• Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format 	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• A certified/signed copy of a Master of Science certificate. 	
• List of publications.   Deadline for applications: 30 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

   

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.
